According to the \emph{Lebesgue's Monotone Convergence} theorem, we only need to prove that $$\forall\ p \ge 1,\ \ \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mathbb{E}[Y_{n}|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]\right]^{p}:=M(p)<+\infty.$$
nodes.statement_short: Normalize Y_n = X_n/2M and reduce to bounding M(p)

nodes.name: Moment recursion
nodes.statement_short: Derive M(p) <= c + C_p M(p/2)

nodes.name: Justify steps
nodes.statement: In the above derivation, Inequality $(a)$ requires noting that $\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}Y_{n}=\frac{1}{2}.$ Inequality $(b)$ uses the \emph{AM-GM} inequality, specifically, \[ \bigg(\frac{a+b}{2}\bigg)^{p} \leq \frac{a^{p} + b^{p}}{2}. \] Inequality $(c)$ involves using \emph{Burkholder's} inequality,\footnote{\textbf{
nodes.statement_short: Justify steps (a)-(c)

nodes.name: Burkholder's inequality
nodes.statement: \emph{Burkholder's} inequality}: For any martingale \((M_n, \mathscr{F}_n)\) with \(M_0 = 0\) almost surely, and for any \(1 \leq p < \infty\), there exist constants \(c_p > 0\) and \(C_p > 0\) depending only on \(p\) such that: \[c_p \, \mathbb{E}[(S(M))^p] \leq \mathbb{E}[(M^*)^p] \leq C_p \, \mathbb{E}[(S(M))^p],\] where \(M^* = \sup_{n \geq 0} |M_n|\) and \(S(M) = \left( \sum_{i \geq 1} (M_i - M_{i-1})^2 \right)^{1/2}\).} where $C_{p}$ is a constant depending only on $p$, and its order with respect to $p$ is $\mathcal{O}(p)$. Inequality $(d)$ requires noting that $$|\mathbb{E}[Y_{n}|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]-Y_{n}|^{2} \leq |\mathbb{E}[Y_{n}|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]-Y_{n}|.$$
nodes.statement_short: State Burkholder's inequality and justify step (d)

nodes.name: Iterate
nodes.statement: By repeatedly using Equation (\ref{iteration}) and using the fact that $C_{p} = \mathcal{O}(p)$, we obtain the following estimate \[ M(p) = o(p^{\sqrt{p}}), \] that is, \[\mathbb{E}[\Lambda^{p}]=o((2M)^{p}\cdot p^{\sqrt{p}}). \tag*{\qedhere}\]
nodes.statement_short: Iterate the recursion to get M(p) = o(p^{sqrt p})

nodes.name: Auxiliary function
nodes.statement: Consider the function \[ f(x) = l^x x^{\sqrt{n}}, \] with its derivative \[ f'(x) = l^x x^{\sqrt{n} - 1} (\ln l \cdot x + \sqrt{n}). \]
nodes.statement_short: Consider f(x)=l^x x^{sqrt n} and its derivative

nodes.name: Head of the sum
nodes.statement: We observe that \( f \) is decreasing for \( x > \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\ln \frac{1}{l}} \). Therefore, we have the following estimate \[ 0 \leq \sum_{0 \leq k \leq \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\ln \frac{1}{l}} + 1} l^k k^{\sqrt{n}} \leq \left( \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\ln \frac{1}{l}} + 1 \right)^{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} l^k = \frac{1}{1 - l} \left( \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\ln \frac{1}{l}} + 1 \right)^{\sqrt{n}} = O\left( \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\ln \frac{1}{l}} \right)^{\sqrt{n}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound the sum up to the maximizer

nodes.name: Tail lower bound
nodes.statement: On the other hand, we can bound the remainder as follows: \[ \begin{aligned} \sum_{k > \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\ln \frac{1}{l}} + 1} l^k k^{\sqrt{n}} &\geq \sum_{k > \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\ln \frac{1}{l}} + 1} \int_{k}^{k+1} l^x x^{\sqrt{n}} \, \mathrm{d}x \\ &= \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \int_{k}^{k+1} l^x x^{\sqrt{n}} \, \mathrm{d}x - \sum_{0 \leq k \leq \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\ln \frac{1}{l}} + 1} \int_{k}^{k+1} l^x x^{\sqrt{n}} \, \mathrm{d}x \\ &\geq \int_{0}^{\infty} l^x x^{\sqrt{n}} \, \mathrm{d}x - \left( \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\ln \frac{1}{l}} + 2 \right)^{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \int_{k}^{k+1} l^x \, \mathrm{d}x \\ &= \frac{\Gamma\left( \sqrt{n} + 1 \right)}{\left( \ln \frac{1}{l} \right)^{\sqrt{n} + 1}} + O\left( \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\ln \frac{1}{l}} \right)^{\sqrt{n}}. \end{aligned} \]
nodes.statement_short: Compare the tail with the Gamma integral from below

nodes.name: Tail upper bound
nodes.statement: Similarly, we have the upper bound \[ \begin{aligned} \sum_{k > \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\ln \frac{1}{l}} + 1} l^k k^{\sqrt{n}} &\leq \sum_{k > \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\ln \frac{1}{l}} + 1} \int_{k-1}^{k} l^x x^{\sqrt{n}} \, \mathrm{d}x \\ &= \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \int_{k-1}^{k} l^x x^{\sqrt{n}} \, \mathrm{d}x - \sum_{1 \leq k \leq \frac{\sqrt{n}}{\ln \frac{1}{l}} + 1} \int_{k-1}^{k} l^x x^{\sqrt{n}} \, \mathrm{d}x \\ &\leq \int_{0}^{\infty} l^x x^{\sqrt{n}} \, \mathrm{d}x = \frac{\Gamma\left( \sqrt{n} + 1 \right)}{\left( \ln \frac{1}{l} \right)^{\sqrt{n} + 1}}. \end{aligned} \]
nodes.statement_short: Compare the tail with the Gamma integral from above

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Combining the estimates above, we have \[ \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} l^k k^{\sqrt{n}} \sim \frac{\Gamma\left( \sqrt{n} + 1 \right)}{\left( \ln \frac{1}{l} \right)^{\sqrt{n} + 1}}, \quad n \to \infty. \tag*{\qedhere} \]
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the asymptotic equivalence

nodes.name: (i) almost sure convergence
nodes.statement: (i) Consider the non-negative adapted process \(\{X_n, \mathscr{F}_n\}_{n \geq 1}\) and define the partial sum of conditional expectations as \(\Lambda_{k,T} := \sum_{n=k}^{T} \mathbb{E}[X_n \mid \mathscr{F}_{n-k}]\). First, we compute the expectation of \(\Lambda_{k,T}\) \[ \mathbb{E}[\Lambda_{k,T}] = \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=k}^{T} \mathbb{E}[X_n \mid \mathscr{F}_{n-k}]\right] = \sum_{n=k}^{T} \mathbb{E}[X_n]< \sum_{n=1}^{T} \mathbb{E}[X_n]\leq M. \] Since \(X_n\) are non-negative, we know that \(\Lambda_{k,T}\) is a non-decreasing sequence, and considering that \(\mathbb{E}(\Lambda_{k,T})\ (\forall\ T\ge 1)\) is also bounded by $M$, we apply the \emph{Lebesgue's Monotone Convergence} theorem. Thus, \(\Lambda_{k,T}\) converges almost surely to a limit \(\Lambda^{(k)}\) \[ \Lambda^{(k)} := \lim_{T \to \infty} \Lambda_{k,T} = \sum_{n=k}^{\infty} \mathbb{E}[X_n \mid \mathscr{F}_{n-k}] \quad \text{a.s.} \] This concludes that the sequence of conditional expectation sums converges almost surely.
nodes.statement_short: Monotone convergence for the lagged sums

nodes.name: Partial sums
nodes.statement: (i) Consider the non-negative adapted process \(\{X_n, \mathscr{F}_n\}_{n \geq 1}\) and define the partial sum of conditional expectations as \(\Lambda_{k,T} := \sum_{n=k}^{T} \mathbb{E}[X_n \mid \mathscr{F}_{n-k}]\).
nodes.statement_short: Define Lambda_{k,T}

nodes.name: Expectation bound
nodes.statement: First, we compute the expectation of \(\Lambda_{k,T}\) \[ \mathbb{E}[\Lambda_{k,T}] = \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=k}^{T} \mathbb{E}[X_n \mid \mathscr{F}_{n-k}]\right] = \sum_{n=k}^{T} \mathbb{E}[X_n]< \sum_{n=1}^{T} \mathbb{E}[X_n]\leq M. \]
nodes.statement_short: E[Lambda_{k,T}] < M

nodes.name: Monotone convergence
nodes.statement: Since \(X_n\) are non-negative, we know that \(\Lambda_{k,T}\) is a non-decreasing sequence, and considering that \(\mathbb{E}(\Lambda_{k,T})\ (\forall\ T\ge 1)\) is also bounded by $M$, we apply the \emph{Lebesgue's Monotone Convergence} theorem. Thus, \(\Lambda_{k,T}\) converges almost surely to a limit \(\Lambda^{(k)}\) \[ \Lambda^{(k)} := \lim_{T \to \infty} \Lambda_{k,T} = \sum_{n=k}^{\infty} \mathbb{E}[X_n \mid \mathscr{F}_{n-k}] \quad \text{a.s.} \] This concludes that the sequence of conditional expectation sums converges almost surely.
nodes.statement_short: Hence a.s. convergence

nodes.name: (ii) moment bounds
nodes.statement_short: Residue-class split and Burkholder give moment recursion

nodes.name: Normalize
nodes.statement: (ii) We begin by normalizing \(X_{n}\) by considering the expression \(Y_{n}= \frac{X_{n}}{2M}\). According to the \emph{Lebesgue's Monotone Convergence} theorem, we only need to prove that $$\forall\ p \ge 1,\ \ \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=k}^{\infty}\mathbb{E}[Y_{n}|\mathscr{F}_{n-k}]\right]^{p}:=M_{k}(p)<+\infty.$$
nodes.statement_short: Normalize and reduce to bounding M_k(p)

nodes.name: Moment recursion
nodes.statement_short: Derive the recursion over residue classes

nodes.name: Justify steps
nodes.statement: In the above derivation, Inequality $(a)$ is by noting that $\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}Y_{n}=\frac{1}{2}.$ Inequality $(b)$ uses the \emph{AM-GM} inequality, specifically, \[ \bigg(\frac{a+b}{2}\bigg)^{p} \leq \frac{a^{p} + b^{p}}{2}. \] Inequality $(c)$ involves using the \emph{AM-GM} inequality for $k$ variables, specifically, \[\left(\frac{a_{1}+a_{2}+...+a_{k}}{k}\right)^{p}\le \left(\frac{a_{1}^{p}+a_{2}^{p}+...+a_{k}^{p}}{k}\right).\] Inequality $(e)$ involves using \emph{Burkholder's} inequality, where $C_{p}$ is a constant depending only on $p$, and its order with respect to $p$ is $\mathcal{O}(p)$. Inequality $(d)$ is by noting that $$|\mathbb{E}[Y_{n}|\mathscr{F}_{n-k}]-Y_{n}|^{2} \leq |\mathbb{E}[Y_{n}|\mathscr{F}_{n-k}]-Y_{n}|.$$
nodes.statement_short: Justify steps (a)-(e) incl. Burkholder

nodes.name: Iterate
nodes.statement: By repeatedly using Equation (\ref{iteration2}) and using the fact that $C_{p} = \mathcal{O}(p)$, we obtain the following estimate \[ M(p) = o((kp)^{\sqrt{p}}), \] that is, \[\mathbb{E}[(\Lambda^{(k)})^{p}]=o((2M)^{p}\cdot (kp)^{\sqrt{p}}).\]
nodes.statement_short: Iterate to M(p) = o((kp)^{sqrt p})

nodes.name: (iii) decomposition of Lambda(l)
nodes.statement: (iii) For any \(0 < l < 1\), we obtain: \begin{align*} \Lambda(l)&=\sum_{k=1}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{t=k}^{+\infty}l^{t-k}X_{t}\right)\bigg|\mathscr{F}_{k-1}\right]=\sum_{k=1}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{t=0}^{+\infty}l^{t}X_{k+t}\right)\bigg|\mathscr{F}_{k-1}\right]\\&=\sum_{t=0}^{+\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[l^{t}X_{k+t}\bigg|\mathscr{F}_{k-1}\right]=\sum_{t=0}^{+\infty}l^{t}\Lambda^{(t)}. \end{align*} Next, we apply Hölder's inequality, we obtain $\forall\ n\ge 2$ \begin{align*} \Lambda(l)^{n}&=\left(\sum_{t=0}^{+\infty}l^{t}\Lambda^{(t)}\right)^{n}\le \left(\frac{1}{1-l}\right)^{n-1}\sum_{t=0}^{+\infty}l^{t}(\Lambda^{(t)})^{n}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Write Lambda(l) as sum l^t Lambda^{(t)} and apply Holder

nodes.name: (iv) exponential moments
nodes.statement: (iv) Then we have: \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[e^{p\Lambda(l)}] & = \sum_{n=0}^{+\infty} \frac{p^{n}\mathbb{E}[\Lambda(l)^n]}{n!}\le\sum_{n=0}^{+\infty} \left(\frac{p}{1-l}\right)^{n}\frac{\sum_{t=0}^{+\infty}l^{t}(\Lambda^{(t)})^{n}}{n!} =\sum_{n=0}^{+\infty} \sum_{t=0}^{+\infty}l^{t}(\Lambda^{(t)})^{n}\left(\frac{p}{1-l}\right)^{n}\frac{1}{n!} \\&\mathop{=}^{(iii)}\mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{n=0}^{+\infty} \sum_{t=0}^{+\infty}l^{t}(2M)^{n}\cdot (tp)^{\sqrt{n}}\left(\frac{p}{1-l}\right)^{n}\frac{1}{n!}\right)\\&=\mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{n=0}^{+\infty} \left(\sum_{t=0}^{+\infty}l^{t}t^{\sqrt{n}}\right)\left(\frac{p}{1-l}\right)^{n}\frac{(2M)^{n}\cdot (p)^{\sqrt{n}}}{n!}\right)\\&\mathop{=}^{\text{Lemma \ref{esti}}}\mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{n=0}^{+\infty} \Gamma(\sqrt{n}+1)\frac{1}{\left( \ln \frac{1}{l} \right)^{\sqrt{n} + 1}}\left(\frac{p}{1-l}\right)^{n}\frac{(2M)^{n}\cdot (p)^{\sqrt{n}}}{n!}\right). \end{align*} By substituting the factorial in the denominator with Stirling's approximation, it is evident that the series inside the $\mathcal{O}$ notation converges and depends only on $p,\ l$ and $M$. The lemma follows.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the exponential and use Lemma B.4 and Stirling

nodes.name: L-smooth expansion
nodes.statement: By the $L$-smoothness in Assumption \ref{ass_2}, we have: \begin{align*} f(u_{t+1})-f(u_{t})\le \nabla f(u_{t})^{\top}(u_{t+1}-u_{t})+\frac{L_{f}}{2}\|u_{t+1}-u_{t}\|^{2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the L-smooth upper bound to f(u_{t+1})-f(u_t)

nodes.name: Substitute u-recursion
nodes.statement_short: Insert Eq. (4), split into Theta_{t,1..4}

nodes.name: Decompose Theta_{t,1}
nodes.statement_short: Split Theta_{t,1} into descent, error Theta_{t,1,1} and martingale M_{t,1}

nodes.name: Bound Theta_{t,1,1}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the error term via conditional expectations

nodes.name: Justify steps
nodes.statement: In the above derivation, in step $(a)$, we utilized the property of conditional expectation, which states that for random variables \(X \in \mathscr{F}_{n-1}\) and \(Y \in \mathscr{F}_{n}\), we have \(\mathbb{E}[XY|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}] = X\mathbb{E}[Y|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]\). Additionally, note that \(\Delta_{t,i} = \sqrt{\Delta_{t,i}}\sqrt{\Delta_{t,i}} < \sqrt{\eta_{v_{t-1}}}\sqrt{\Delta_{t,i}}\) (due to Property \ref{property_0}, we know \(\Delta_{t,i} \ge 0\), so taking the square root is well-defined). In step $(b)$, we employed the \emph{AM-GM} inequality, which states \(ab \le \frac{a^{2} + b^{2}}{2}\). In step $(c)$, we used the \emph{Cauchy-Schwarz} inequality for conditional expectations, namely \(\mathbb{E}[XY|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}] \le \sqrt{\mathbb{E}[X^{2}|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}] \mathbb{E}[Y^{2}|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]}.\) For step $(d)$, we used Property \ref{property_-1}. Specifically, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^{d}\mathbb{E}[g_{t,i}^{2}|\mathscr{F}_{t-1}]=\mathbb{E}[\|g_{t}\|^{2}|\mathscr{F}_{t-1}]\le (A+2L_{f}B)f(w_{t})+C. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Justify steps via conditional expectation, AM-GM, Cauchy-Schwarz, Property 1

nodes.name: Combine Theta_{t,1}
nodes.statement: Substituting the estimate of $\Theta_{t,1,1}$ into Equation (\ref{adam_2}), we obtain \begin{align*} \Theta_{t,1}&=-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\zeta_{i}(t)+\frac{A+2L_{f}B}{2}\overline{\Delta}_{t}\cdot f(w_t)+C\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}+\underbrace{M_{t,1}+M_{t,2}+M_{t,3}}_{M_{t}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Combine the Theta_{t,1} bound

nodes.name: Pass to u_t
nodes.statement: Then, we use Property \ref{property_2} to replace $f(w_t)$ with $f(u_t)$ to obtain \begin{align} \Theta_{t,1}&=-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\zeta_{i}(t)+\frac{(A+2L_{f}B)(L_{f}+1)}{2}\overline{\Delta}_{t}\cdot f(u_t)+C\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}\notag\\&+\frac{(L_{f}+1)\beta_{1}^{2}}{2(1-\beta_1)^{2}}\|\eta_{v_{t-1}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}+M_{t}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Replace f(w_t) by f(u_t) via Property 5

nodes.name: Bound Theta_{t,2}
nodes.statement_short: Bound Theta_{t,2} by smoothness

nodes.name: Bound Theta_{t,3}
nodes.statement: Next, we handle the term $\Theta_{t,3}$. We have {\begin{align} \Theta_{t,3}&=\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}\nabla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}\le\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}|\nabla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|. \end{align}}
nodes.statement_short: Bound Theta_{t,3} by absolute values

nodes.name: Bound Theta_{t,4}
nodes.statement: For $\Theta_{t,4},$ because $\Delta_{t,i}\le \eta_{v_{t-1},i}$, we obtain that \begin{align} \Theta_{t,4}=\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}^{2}m_{t-1,i}^{2}<\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta^{2}_{v_{t-1},i}m_{t-1,i}^{2}=\|\eta_{v_{t-1}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Delta_{t,i} <= eta_{v_{t-1},i}

nodes.name: Assemble
nodes.statement: Finally, substituting the estimates of $\Theta_{t,1}$ from Equation (\ref{adam_3}), $\Theta_{t,2}$ from Equation (\ref{adam_5}), $\Theta_{t,3}$ from Equation (\ref{adam_11}), and $\Theta_{t,4}$ from Equation (\ref{adam_15}) back into Equation (\ref{adam_-1}), we obtain \begin{align*} &\bigg(\underbrace{{f(u_{t+1})-f^*+C\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}}}_{\hat{f}(u_{t+1})}\bigg)-\bigg(\underbrace{{f(u_{t})-f^*+C\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t-1},i}}}_{\hat{f}(u_{t})}\bigg)\le-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\zeta_{i}(t)+C_{1}\overline{\Delta}_{t}\cdot f(u_{t})\notag\\&+C_{2}\|{\eta_{v_{t-1}}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}+\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}|\nabla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|+(L_{f}+1)\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}+M_{t}, \end{align*} where \begin{align} &C_{1}:=\frac{(A+2L_{f}B)(L_{f}+1)}{2},\ \ C_{2}:=\frac{\beta_{1}^{2}L_{f}^{2}}{2(1-\beta_{1})^{2}}+L_{f}\Big(\frac{\beta_{1}}{1-\beta_{1}}\Big)^{2}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Substitute all four bounds to get the f-hat inequality

nodes.name: Absorb f(u_t)
nodes.statement: To the second term on the right side of the above inequality, we apply the inequality $\$[f(u_{t}) < f(u_{t})-f^* + C\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t-1},i}=\hat{f}(u_{t})$ and then move the expanded term to the left side of the inequality. This obtains \begin{align*} \hat{f}(u_{t+1})-(1+C_{1}\overline{\Delta}_{t})\hat{f}(u_{t})\le& -\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\zeta_{i}(t)+C_{1}\overline{\Delta}_{t}\cdot f(u_{t})\notag\\&\ +C_{2}\|{\eta_{v_{t-1}}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}+\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}|\nabla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|\\&\ +(L_{f}+1)\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}+M_{t}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Move the C_1 Delta-bar f-hat term to the left side

nodes.name: Discounted Delta-bar
nodes.statement: Next, we define \begin{align*} \overline{\Delta}_{\sqrt{\beta_{1}},k} := \sum_{i=1}^{d}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=k}^{+\infty} (\sqrt{\beta_{1}})^{t-k} \Delta_{t,i}\bigg|\mathscr{F}_{k-1}\right]. \end{align*} Observe that \[1 + C_{1} \overline{\Delta}_{t} \leq 1 + \left(\frac{D_1}{1 - \sqrt{\beta_{1}}} + 1\right) \overline{\Delta}_{\sqrt{\beta_{1}},t},\] where \(D_{1}\) is defined in Lemma \ref{property_3.510}. Thus, we have \begin{align*} \hat{f}(u_{t+1})-\left(1 + \left(\frac{D_1}{1 - \sqrt{\beta_{1}}} + 1\right) \overline{\Delta}_{\sqrt{\beta_{1}},t}\right)\hat{f}(u_{t})\le& -\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\zeta_{i}(t)+C_{1}\overline{\Delta}_{t}\cdot f(u_{t})\notag\\&\ +C_{2}\|{\eta_{v_{t-1}}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}+\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}|\nabla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|\\&\ +(L_{f}+1)\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}+M_{t}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Define Delta-bar_{sqrt beta_1,k} and dominate C_1 Delta-bar_t

nodes.name: Product Pi_{Delta,t}
nodes.statement: Next, we construct an auxiliary variable \begin{align*} \Pi_{\Delta,t}:=\prod_{k=1}^{t}\left(1+\left(\frac{D_1}{1-\sqrt{\beta_{1}}}+1\right)\overline{\Delta}_{\sqrt{\beta_{1}},k}\right)^{-1}\ (t\ge 1),\ \Pi_{\Delta,0}:=1. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Construct the product weight Pi_{Delta,t}

nodes.name: Multiply and conclude
nodes.statement: Multiplying both sides of the above inequality by $\Pi_{\Delta,t},$ we obtain \begin{align*} \Pi_{\Delta,t}\hat{f}(u_{t+1})-\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})\le &-\frac{1}{2}\Pi_{\Delta,t}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\zeta_{i}(t)\notag+C_{2}\|{\eta_{v_{t-1}}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}+\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}|\nabla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|\\&\ +(L_{f}+1)\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}+\Pi_{\Delta,t}M_{t}. \end{align*} With the inequality, we complete the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Multiply by Pi_{Delta,t} to obtain the lemma

nodes.name: Expand sqrt(S_T)
nodes.statement: For any $\phi \in \mathbb{R}$, we consider $\frac{\sqrt{S_{T}}}{(T+1)^{\phi}}$. We have \begin{align*} \frac{\sqrt{S_{T}}}{(T+1)^{\phi}}&=\frac{{S_{T}}}{(T+1)^{\phi}\sqrt{S_{T}}}=\frac{S_{0}+\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|g_{t}\|^{2}}{(T+1)^{\phi}\sqrt{S_{T}}} =\frac{S_{0}}{(T+1)^{\phi}\sqrt{S_{T}}} +\sum_{t=1}^{T}\frac{\|g_{t}\|^{2}}{(T+1)^{\phi}\sqrt{S_{T}}}\\&\le \frac{S_{0}}{(T+1)^{\phi}\sqrt{S_{T}}} +\sum_{t=1}^{T}\frac{\|g_{t}\|^{2}}{(T+1)^{\phi}\sqrt{S_{T}}}\le {\sqrt{S_{0}}}+\sum_{t=1}^{T}\frac{\|g_{t}\|^{2}}{(t+1)^{\phi}\sqrt{S_{t-1}}}\\&={\sqrt{dv}}+\sum_{t=1}^{T}\frac{\|g_{t}\|^{2}}{(t+1)^{\phi}\sqrt{S_{t-1}}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite and bound sqrt(S_T)/(T+1)^phi

nodes.name: Multiply by Pi
nodes.statement: By multiplying both sides of the above inequality by \(\Pi_{\Delta,T}\) and noting the monotonicity of \(\{\Pi_{\Delta,t}\}_{t \geq 1}\) as well as the fact that \(\Pi_{\Delta,T} \leq 1\) for all \(T \geq 1\), the lemma follows.
nodes.statement_short: Multiply by the monotone Pi_{Delta,T} <= 1

nodes.name: Apply Lemma C.3 with phi=4
nodes.statement: We take $\phi = 4$ in Lemma \ref{vital_1} and bound the expectation of the partial sum $\sum_{t=1}^{T}\Lambda_{4,t}$. We have \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Lambda_{4,t}\Bigg]&=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Lambda_{4,t}]=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\frac{\Pi_{\Delta,t}\|g_{t}\|^{2}}{(t+1)^{4}\sqrt{S_{t-1}}}\Bigg]=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\frac{\Pi_{\Delta,t}\mathbb{E}[\|g_{t}\|^{2}|\mathscr{F}_{t-1}]}{(t+1)^{4}\sqrt{S_{t-1}}}\Bigg]\notag\\&\mathop{\le}^{\text{Property \ref{property_-1}}}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\frac{(A+2L_{f}B)\Pi_{\Delta,t}(f(w_{t})-f^*)+C}{(t+1)^{4}\sqrt{S_{t-1}}}\Bigg]\notag\\&\le C_{3}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\frac{1}{(t+1)^{4}}\mathbb{E}\left[\Pi_{\Delta,t}(f(w_{t})-f^*)\right]+C_{4}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\frac{1}{(t+1)^{4}}, \end{align} where $$C_{3}:=\frac{A+2L_{f}B}{\sqrt{S_{0}}},\ C_{4}:=\frac{C}{\sqrt{S_{0}}}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Bound the expected weighted sum using Property 1

nodes.name: Lemma C.2
nodes.statement: Based on the results in Lemma \ref{lem_sum'}, we can compute: \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\left[\Pi_{\Delta,t}(f(w_{t})-f^*)\right]=\mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{k=1}^{t}\mathbb{E}\|\eta_{v_{k}}\circ g_{k}\|^{2}\right)+\mathcal{O}(1)=\mathcal{O}(t). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: E[Pi(f-f*)] = O(t)

nodes.name: Summability
nodes.statement: Substitute the above result into Equation (\ref{dsacdqewed}), and combine $\forall\ p\ge 2$ \[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\frac{1}{(t+1)^{p}}\le\sum_{t=1}^{T}\frac{1}{(t+1)^{2}}\le \sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\frac{1}{t^{2}}=\frac{\pi^{2}}{6}.\] We get \[\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Lambda_{4,t}\Bigg]=\mathcal{O}(1).\]
nodes.statement_short: The weighted sum has bounded expectation

nodes.name: Monotone convergence
nodes.statement: It can be observed that the right-hand side of the above inequality is independent of $T$. Thus, according to the \emph{Lebesgue's Monotone Convergence} theorem, we have \[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Lambda_{4,t} \to \sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Lambda_{4,t} \quad \text{a.s.},\] and \[ \mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Lambda_{4,t}\Bigg] = \lim_{T \to \infty} \mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Lambda_{4,t}\Bigg] = \lim_{T \to \infty} \sum_{t=1}^{T} \mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Lambda_{4,t}] =\mathcal{O}(1). \]
nodes.statement_short: The infinite sum converges a.s. with finite mean

nodes.name: Define zeta
nodes.statement: By setting $$\zeta := \sqrt{dv} + \sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Lambda_{4,t},$$ and combining Lemma \ref{vital_1}, we have \begin{align} \sqrt{S_{T}}\le \Pi_{\Delta,T}^{-1} (T+1)^{4}\zeta<\Pi_{\Delta,\infty}^{-1} (T+1)^{4}\zeta. \end{align} Meanwhile, \begin{align} \mathbb{E}[\zeta]=\sqrt{dv}+\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\Lambda_{4,t}\Bigg]=\mathcal{O}(1).\end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Define zeta and derive sqrt(S_T) bound and E[zeta]=O(1)

nodes.name: Logarithmic bound
nodes.statement: Then through Equation (\ref{power}), we have \begin{align*} \frac{1}{2}\ln\left(\frac{S_{T}}{v}\right)&\le 4\ln(T+1)+\ln\left(\Pi_{\Delta,\infty}^{-1}\zeta\right)\\&\le4\ln(T+1)+\ln\left(\max\left\{e,\Pi_{\Delta,\infty}^{-1}\zeta\right\}\right)\\&\le 4\ln(T+1)\left(1+\frac{\ln\left(\max\left\{e,\Pi_{\Delta,\infty}^{-1}\zeta\right\}\right)}{4\ln(T+1)}\right)\\&\mathop{\le}^{\ln(T+1)\ge 1/2}4\ln(T+1)\left(1+\frac{1}{2}{\ln\left(\max\left\{e,\Pi_{\Delta,\infty}^{-1}\zeta\right\}\right)}\right). \end{align*} The lemma follows
nodes.statement_short: Take logarithms to bound ln(S_T/v)

nodes.name: Lemma C.2
nodes.statement: According to the second conclusion of Lemma \ref{lem_sum'}, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\left[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\zeta_{i}(t)\right]=\mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\|\eta_{v_{t}}\circ g_{t}\|^{2}\right)+\mathcal{O}(1). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce via the second conclusion of Lemma C.2

nodes.name: Bound per-step energy
nodes.statement: To prove the conclusion of this lemma, we only need to bound $\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\|\eta_{v_{t}}\circ g_{t}\|^{2}.$ Specifically, \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\|\eta_{v_{t}}\circ g_{t}\|^{2}&=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}\right]=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{i=1}^{d}\frac{\eta_{t}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}}{(\sqrt{v_{t,i}}+\mu)^{2}}\right]\le \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{i=1}^{d}\frac{1}{t^{2\delta}}\frac{g_{t,i}^{2}}{{tv_{t,i}}}\right]\notag\\&\mathop{\le}^{\text{Property \ref{property_1}}}\frac{(t+1)^{2\delta}}{t^{2\delta}}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{i=1}^{d}\frac{1}{\alpha_{1}(t+1)^{2\delta}}\frac{g_{t,i}^{2}}{{S_{t,i}}}\right]\\ &\mathop{\le}^{(a)}\frac{2^{2\delta}}{\alpha_{1}}{\zeta}^{\frac{\delta}{2}}\Pi^{-\frac{\delta}{2}}_{\Delta,\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\frac{g_{t,i}^{2}}{{S_{t,i}}^{1+\frac{\delta}{4}}}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound E||eta_{v_t} o g_t||^2 using Property 3

nodes.name: Lemma C.4
nodes.statement: In step $(a)$ of the above derivation, we apply Lemma \ref{vital_0} to $(t+1)^{2\delta}$. Specifically, according to Lemma \ref{vital_0}, we have \begin{align*} \sqrt{S_{t}}\le \Pi_{\Delta,\infty}^{-1}(t+1)^{4}\zeta. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use the S_t bound of Lemma C.4

nodes.name: Series-integral comparison
nodes.statement: Next, with the estimate for $\mathbb{E}\|\eta_{v_{t}}\circ g_{t}\|^{2}$, we can estimate $\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\|\eta_{v_{t}}\circ g_{t}\|^{2}$. To achieve this, note that \begin{align} \sum_{t=1}^{T} \mathbb{E}\|\eta_{v_{t}}\circ g_{t}\|^{2}&=\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{2^{2\delta}}{\alpha_{1}}{\zeta}^{\frac{\delta}{2}}\Pi^{-\frac{\delta}{2}}_{\Delta,\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\frac{g_{t,i}^{2}}{{S_{t,i}}^{1+\frac{\delta}{4}}}\right]\le \mathbb{E}\left[\frac{2^{2\delta}}{\alpha_{1}}{\zeta}^{\frac{\delta}{2}}\Pi^{-\frac{\delta}{2}}_{\Delta,\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\int_{S_{0,i}}^{S_{T,i}}\frac{1}{{x}^{1+\frac{\delta}{4}}}\text{d}x\right]\notag\\&\le \begin{cases} \frac{2^{2\delta}}{\alpha_{1}}\mathbb{E}\left[{\zeta}^{\frac{\delta}{4}}\Pi^{-\frac{\delta}{2}}_{\Delta,\infty}\right], & \text{if } \delta \in (0,1] \\ \frac{2^{2\delta}}{\alpha_{1}}\mathbb{E}\left[\ln\big(\frac{S_{T}}{dv}\big)\right], & \text{if } \delta = 0 \end{cases}\notag\\&\mathop{\le}^{(b)}\begin{cases} \mathcal{O}(1), & \text{if } \delta \in (0,1] \\ \frac{d2^{2\delta}}{\alpha_{1}}\mathbb{E}\left[\ln\big(\frac{S_{T}}{dv}\big)\right], & \text{if } \delta = 0 \end{cases}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Sum over t and compare with an integral

nodes.name: Holder
nodes.statement: In step $(b)$, we used the following inequality, i.e. the \emph{Hölder's} inequality, to obtain the $\mathcal{O}(1)$ result \[\mathbb{E}\left[{\zeta}^{\frac{\delta}{4}}\Pi^{-\frac{\delta}{2}}_{\Delta,\infty}\right]\le \mathbb{E}^{\delta/4}\left[\zeta\right]\cdot\mathbb{E}^{\frac{4-\delta}{4}}\left[\Pi^{-\frac{2\delta}{4-\delta}}_{\Delta,\infty}\right]\mathop{\le}^{\text{Lemma \ref{bounded_moment} and \ref{vital_0}}} C_{\zeta}^{\delta/4}.C_{v,d,\frac{2\delta}{4-\delta}}^{\frac{4-\delta}{4}}=\mathcal{O}(1).\] This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Holder with Lemmas C.1 and C.4 gives O(1)

nodes.name: Reduce to delta=0; recall Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: We only present the case where $\delta = 0$. The case where $\delta > 0$ can be treated using exactly the same approach. Recall the approximate descent inequality (Lemma \ref{sufficient:decrease}) \begin{align*} \Pi_{\Delta,t}\hat{f}(u_{t+1})-\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})\le& -\frac{1}{2}\Pi_{\Delta,t}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\zeta_{i}(t)\notag+C_{2}\|{\eta_{v_{t-1}}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}+\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}|\nabla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|\\&\ +(L_{f}+1)\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}+\Pi_{\Delta,t}M_{t}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Treat delta=0 and recall the approximate descent inequality

nodes.name: Normalize by ln^2
nodes.statement: We divide both sides of the above inequality by $\ln^{2}(t+1)$. Noticing that $\ln^{2}(t+1) < \ln^{2}(t+2)$, we obtain \begin{align} \frac{\Pi_{\Delta,t}\hat{f}(u_{t+1})}{\ln^{2}(t+2)}-\frac{\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})}{\ln^{2}(t+1)}&\le C_{2}\frac{\|{\eta_{v_{t-1}}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}}{\ln^{2}(t+1)}+\sum_{i=1}^{d}\frac{\Delta_{t,i}|\nabla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|}{\ln^{2}(t+1)}\\&+(L_{f}+1)\sum_{i=1}^{d}\frac{\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}}{\ln^{2}(t+1)}+\Pi_{\Delta,t}\frac{M_{t}}{\ln^{2}(t+1)}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Divide by ln^2(t+1)

nodes.name: Define Omega_t
nodes.statement_short: Collect error terms into Omega_t

nodes.name: Estimate sum of Omega
nodes.statement: For the term \(\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty} \mathbb{E}[\Omega_{t}]\), we can estimate it as \begin{align*} \sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}[\Omega_{t}]:=&\ C_{2}\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\frac{\mathbb{E}\|{\eta_{v_{t-1}}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}}{\ln^{t+1}}+\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\frac{\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{t,i}|\nabla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|]}{\ln^{2}(t+1)}\\&\ +(L_{f}+1)\sum_{i=1}^{d}\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\frac{\mathbb{E}[\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}]}{\ln^{2}(t+1)}\\ \mathop{\le}^{(a)} &\ \mathcal{O}(1)+\sum_{i=1}^{d}\mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{\mathbb{E}[\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}]}{\ln^{2}(t+1)}\right]\right)\\ \mathop{\le}^{(b)} &\ \mathcal{O}(1)+\sum_{i=1}^{d}\mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{t=1,S_{t,i}>2v}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\zeta'^{2}\frac{\mathbb{E}[\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}]}{\ln^{2}\left(S_{t,i}/v\right)}\right]\right). \end{align*} In step $(a)$, we use Property \ref{property_3} and Lemma \ref{lem_sum'}. In step $(b)$, we use the last result from Lemma \ref{vital_0}, which states $$\ln\Big(\frac{S_{t,i}}{v}\Big)\le\ln\Big(\frac{S_{t}}{v}\Big)\le \zeta'\ln (T+1).$$
nodes.statement_short: Use Property 4, Lemma C.2 and Lemma C.4

nodes.name: Series-integral bound
nodes.statement: Then, using the series-integral inequality, we bound $\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty} \mathbb{E}[\Omega_{t}]$ and obtain \begin{align*} \sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}[\Omega_{t}]&\le \mathcal{O}(1)+\mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{d}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\sum_{t=1,S_{t,i}>2v}^{+\infty}\frac{({\zeta'}^{2})\frac{g_{t,i}^{2}}{v}}{\ln^{2}(\frac{S_{t,i}}{v})\frac{S_{t,i}}{v}}\bigg]\right)\\ & <\mathcal{O}(1)+\mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{d}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\int_{2}^{+\infty}\frac{{\zeta'}^{2}}{x\ln^{2}x}\text{d}x\Bigg]\right)\\&=\mathcal{O}(1)+\mathcal{O}(\mathbb{E}[\zeta'^{2}]). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound by an integral of 1/(x ln^2 x)

nodes.name: Moment of zeta'
nodes.statement: Next, we use the explicit expression for $\zeta'$ given in Lemma \ref{vital_0} to bound $\mathbb{E}[{\zeta'}^{2}]$. We have: \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[{\zeta'}^{2}]&=\mathbb{E}\left[16\left(1+\frac{1}{2}{\ln\left(\max\left\{e,\Pi_{\Delta,\infty}^{-1}\zeta\right\}\right)}\right)\right]<+\infty. \end{align*} As a result, we have \begin{align} \sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}[\Omega_{t}]<+\infty. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: E[zeta'^2] finite, so sum E[Omega_t] < infinity

nodes.name: Conditional summability
nodes.statement: According to the \emph{Lebesgue's Monotone Convergence} theorem, we know that the above result implies \begin{align} \sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\mathbb{E}[\Omega_{t}|\mathscr{F}_{t-1}]<+\infty\ \ \text{a.s.} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Sum of conditional expectations of Omega_t finite a.s.

nodes.name: Supermartingale inequality
nodes.statement: Next, we take the conditional expectation with respect to $\mathscr{F}_{t-1}$ on both sides of Equation (\ref{adam_7980}), which obtains \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\Bigg[\frac{\Pi_{\Delta,t+1}\hat{f}(u_{t+1})}{\ln^{2}(t+2)}\Bigg|\mathscr{F}_{t-1}\Bigg]\le \frac{\Pi_{\Delta,t}\hat{f}(u_{t})}{\ln^{2}(t+1)}+\mathbb{E}[{\Omega_{t}}|\mathscr{F}_{t-1}]+0. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Take conditional expectation of the normalized inequality

nodes.name: Supermartingale convergence
nodes.statement: Based on the result from Equation (\ref{adam_7982}) and the \emph{Supermartingale Convergence} theorem, we deduce that $\frac{\Pi_{\Delta,t}\hat{f}(u_{t})}{\ln^{2}(t+1)}$ converges almost surely. Then, according to Property \ref{property_2}, we bound ${f}(w_{t})-f^*$ using $\hat{f}(u_{t}).$ This concludes our first result.
nodes.statement_short: Supermartingale convergence and Property 5 give the a.s. bound

nodes.name: Expectation recursion
nodes.statement: Next, we take the expectation on both sides of Equation (\ref{adam_7980}), which yields \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\Bigg[\frac{\Pi_{\Delta,t+1}\hat{f}(u_{t+1})}{\ln^{2}(t+2)}\Bigg]\le \mathbb{E}\Bigg[\frac{\Pi_{\Delta,t}\hat{f}(u_{t})}{\ln^{2}(t+1)}\Bigg]+\mathbb{E}[{\Omega_{t}}]+0. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Take expectations of the normalized inequality

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Based on the convergence result of the expectation summation in Equation (\ref{adam_7981}) and a summation formula for a recursive sequence, we conclude our second result. Thus, the analysis for the case $\delta = 0$ has been completed. The case $\delta > 0$ could be analyzed using the same method, which concludes the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the recursion for the expectation bound

nodes.name: Holder split
nodes.statement: Since the case of $\delta > 0$ is relatively straightforward, we first analyze the scenario where $\delta > 0$. According to the second conclusion for $\delta > 0$ in Lemma \ref{lem_g}, we obtain \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[{S^{3/4}_{T}}]=\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,T}^{-3/4}\Pi^{3/4}_{\Delta,T}S^{3/4}_{T}]\mathop{\le}^{\text{\emph{Hölder's} inequality}} \mathbb{E}^{1/4}[\Pi_{\Delta,T}^{-3}]\mathbb{E}^{3/4}[\Pi_{\Delta,T}S_{T}]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: For delta>0, split E[S_T^{3/4}] with Holder

nodes.name: Bound both factors
nodes.statement: Then according to Lemma \ref{bounded_moment}, we have $\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,T}^{-3}] \leq C_{v,d,3}$. For the other term, $\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,T} S_{T}]$, we can handle the term as follows. \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,T} S_{T}]&\le S_{0}+\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\Pi_{\Delta,T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|g_{t}\|^{2}\Bigg] \le dv+ \mathbb{E}\Bigg[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\Pi_{\Delta,T}\|g_{t}\|^{2}\Bigg] \\&=dv+ \sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\big[\Pi_{\Delta,T}\mathbb{E}[\|g_{t}\|^{2}|\mathscr{F}_{t-1}]\big]\\& \mathop{\le}^{\text{Property \ref{property_-1}}}dv+ \sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\big[\Pi_{\Delta,T}((A+2L_{f}B)(f(w_{t})-f^{*})+C)\big]\\&\mathop{\le}^{\text{Lemma \ref{lem_g}}}dv+((A+2L_{f}B)M_{\delta}+C)T. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma C.1 and Property 1 with Lemma C.7

nodes.name: Rate for delta>0
nodes.statement: This implies \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[\sqrt{S_{T}}]\le {C^{1/4}_{v,d,3}}(dv+((A+2L_{f}B)M_{\delta}+C)T^{3/4}=\mathcal{O}({T^{3/4}}). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Obtain O(T^{3/4})

nodes.name: Case delta=0
nodes.statement: For the case where $\delta = 0$, we use the same approach as in the case of $\delta > 0$ and apply the corresponding conclusion for $\delta = 0$ from Lemma \ref{lem_g}. Thus, we obtain \[\mathbb{E}[{S^{3/4}_{T}}]=\mathcal{O}({T^{3/4}}\ln^{3/2} T). \tag*{\qedhere}\]
nodes.statement_short: Same argument with the delta=0 part of Lemma C.7

nodes.name: Case lambda=1
nodes.statement: We discuss two cases based on the value of $\lambda$. In the first case, when $\lambda = 1$, we have \begin{align*} v_{t+1}=\Big(1-\frac{1}{t+1}\Big)v_{t}+\frac{1}{t+1}g_{t}^{\circ 2}\ (\forall\ t\ge 1), \end{align*} that is \[(t+1)v_{t+1}=tv_{t}+g_{t}^{\circ 2}.\] Summing over all the coordinates, we obtain \begin{align} (t+1)\Sigma_{v_{t+1}}=t\Sigma_{v_{t}}+\|g_{t}\|^{2}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Recursion (t+1)Sigma_{v_{t+1}} = t Sigma_{v_t} + ||g_t||^2

nodes.name: Weight by Pi
nodes.statement: Multiplying both sides of the above equation by $\Pi_{\Delta,t}$, and noting that $\Pi_{\Delta,t} \geq \Pi_{\Delta,t+1}$, we have \[(t+1)\Pi_{\Delta,t+1}\Sigma_{v_{t+1}}=t\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}+\Pi_{\Delta,t}\|g_{t}\|^{2}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Multiply by Pi_{Delta,t}

nodes.name: Expectation
nodes.statement: Taking the expectation on both sides, we obtain \begin{align*} (t+1)\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t+1}\Sigma_{v_{t+1}}]&\le t\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}]+\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\|g_{t}\|^{2}]\\&=t\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}]+\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\mathbb{E}[\|g_{t}\|^{2}|\mathscr{F}_{t-1}]]\\&\mathop{\le}^{\text{Property \ref{property_-1}}}t\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}]+(A+2L_{f}B)\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}(f(w_{t})-f^*)]+C\\&\le t\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}]+(A+2L_{f}B)\Big(\sup_{t\ge 1}\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}(f(w_{t})-f^*)]\Big)+C \\&\mathop{\le}^{\text{Lemma \ref{lem_g}}}t\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}]+(A+2L_{f}B)M_{\delta}+C. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use Property 1 and Lemma C.7

nodes.name: Iterate
nodes.statement: By iterating the above inequality, we finally have \[ (t+1)\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t+1}\Sigma_{v_{t+1}}]\le \begin{cases} \mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,2}\Sigma_{v_{1}}]+\big((A+2L_{f}B)M_{\delta}+C\big)t, & \text{if } \delta \in (0,1] \\ \mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,2}\Sigma_{v_{1}}]+\big((A+2L_{f}B)M_{0}\ln^{2}t+C\big)t, & \text{if } \delta = 0 \end{cases}. \] This implies that for any $t \geq 1$, \[\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t+1}\Sigma_{v_{t+1}}]\le \begin{cases} \mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,2}\Sigma_{v_{1}}]+(A+2L_{f}B)M_{\delta}+C, & \text{if } \delta \in (0,1] \\ \mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,2}\Sigma_{v_{1}}]+(A+2L_{f}B)M_{0}\ln^{2}t+C, & \text{if } \delta = 0 \end{cases},\] that is \begin{align*} \sup_{t\ge 1}\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}]<\begin{cases} \mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,2}\Sigma_{v_{1}}]+(A+2L_{f}B)M_{\delta}+C, & \text{if } \delta \in (0,1] \\ \mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,2}\Sigma_{v_{1}}]+(A+2L_{f}B)M_{0}\ln^{2}t+C, & \text{if } \delta = 0 \end{cases}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Iterate to the uniform bound

nodes.name: Case lambda>1
nodes.statement: Next, we discuss the scenario when $\lambda > 1$. In this case, we have the following inequality. \[\Sigma_{v_{t+1}}\le \Sigma_{v_{t}}+\frac{1}{(t+1)^{\lambda}}\|g_{t}\|^{2}.\] We multiply both sides of the above inequality by $\Pi_{\Delta,t}$ and, noting its monotonicity, we have \begin{align} \Pi_{\Delta,t+1}\Sigma_{v_{t+1}}\le \Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}+\frac{\Pi_{\Delta,t}}{(t+1)^{\lambda}}\|g_{t}\|^{2}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Recursion with weight 1/(t+1)^lambda

nodes.name: Conditional expectation
nodes.statement: Taking the conditional expectation with respect to $\mathscr{F}_{t-1}$ on both sides of the inequality, we have \[ \mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t+1}\Sigma_{v_{t+1}}|\mathscr{F}_{t-1}]\le \Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}+\frac{\Pi_{\Delta,t}}{(t+1)^{\lambda}}\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\|g_{t}\|^{2}|\mathscr{F}_{t-1}]. \] According to Property \ref{property_-1} and Lemma \ref{lem_g}, we obtain \begin{align*} &\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\frac{\Pi_{\Delta,t}}{(t+1)^{\lambda}}\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\|g_{t}\|^{2}|\mathscr{F}_{t-1}]\\\le & \begin{cases} \big((A+2L_{f}B)\sup_{t\ge 1}\big(\Pi_{\Delta,t}(f(w_{t})-f^*)\big)+C\big)\cdot\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\frac{1}{(t+1)^{\lambda}}, & \text{if } \delta \in (0,1] \\ \Big((A+2L_{f}B)\sup_{t\ge 1}\Big(\frac{\Pi_{\Delta,t}(f(w_{t})-f^*)}{\ln^{2}t}\Big)+C\Big)\cdot\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\frac{\ln^{2}t}{(t+1)^{\lambda}}, & \text{if } \delta = 0 \end{cases}\\< & +\infty\ \ \text{a.s.}\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Summable conditional increments via Property 1 and Lemma C.7

nodes.name: Supermartingale convergence
nodes.statement: By the \textit{Supermartingale Convergence theorem}, we obtain that $\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}$ converges almost surely, which implies that $\sup_{t \geq 1} \Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}} < +\infty \ \ \text{a.s.}$ According to Lemma \ref{bounded_moment}, where $\sup_{t \geq 1} \Pi_{\Delta,t}^{-1} < +\infty \ \ \text{a.s.}$, we can immediately deduce that $\sup_{t \geq 1} \Sigma_{v_{t}} < +\infty \ \ \text{a.s.}$
nodes.statement_short: Pi Sigma converges a.s.; with Lemma C.1, Sigma bounded a.s.

nodes.name: Expected supremum
nodes.statement: Next, we prove that the expected supremum is finite. Taking the expectation on both sides of Equation (\ref{adam_-1234321}), we obtain \[ \mathbb{E}\big[\Pi_{\Delta,t+1}\Sigma_{v_{t+1}}\big]\le \mathbb{E}\big[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}\big]+\frac{1}{(t+1)^{\lambda}}\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\|g_{t}\|^{2}]. \] By summing the above recursive inequalities and using the results from Property \ref{property_-1} and Lemma \ref{lem_g}, we can easily prove that \[\sup_{t \geq 1} \mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}] < \begin{cases} \big((A+2L_{f}B)M_{\delta}+C\big)\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\frac{1}{(t+1)^{\lambda}}, & \text{if } \delta \in (0,1] \\ \big((A+2L_{f}B)M_{0}+C\big)\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\frac{\ln^{2}t}{(t+1)^{\lambda}}, & \text{if } \delta = 0 \end{cases}<+\infty.\] With this inequality we complete the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Prove the expected bound

nodes.name: Take expectations
nodes.statement: Taking the expectation on both sides of Equation (\ref{adam_-1234321}), we obtain \[ \mathbb{E}\big[\Pi_{\Delta,t+1}\Sigma_{v_{t+1}}\big]\le \mathbb{E}\big[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}\big]+\frac{1}{(t+1)^{\lambda}}\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\|g_{t}\|^{2}]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Expectation of the recursion

nodes.name: Sum
nodes.statement: By summing the above recursive inequalities and using the results from Property \ref{property_-1} and Lemma \ref{lem_g}, we can easily prove that \[\sup_{t \geq 1} \mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}] < \begin{cases} \big((A+2L_{f}B)M_{\delta}+C\big)\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\frac{1}{(t+1)^{\lambda}}, & \text{if } \delta \in (0,1] \\ \big((A+2L_{f}B)M_{0}+C\big)\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\frac{\ln^{2}t}{(t+1)^{\lambda}}, & \text{if } \delta = 0 \end{cases}<+\infty.\] With this inequality we complete the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Sum and apply Property 1 and Lemma C.7

nodes.name: Lemma C.5
nodes.statement: According to the result from Lemma \ref{lem_sum}, it is straightforward to see that when $\delta > 0$, \begin{align*} \sum_{t=2}^{T}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\frac{\eta_{t-1}\|\nabla f(w_{t})\|^{2}}{\sqrt{\Sigma_{v_{t-1}}+\mu}}\bigg]&\le \sum_{t=2}^{T}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\frac{\eta_{t-1}}{\sqrt{\Sigma_{v_{t-1}}+\mu}}\sum_{i=1}^{d}(\nabla_{i}f(w_{t}))^{2}\bigg]\\&\le \sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\zeta_{i}(t)\bigg]\\&<C_{4,\delta}<+\infty. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the expected weighted gradient sum via Lemma C.5

nodes.name: Monotone convergence
nodes.statement: Next, we apply the \emph{Lebesgue's Monotone Convergence theorem} \[\sum_{t=2}^{+\infty}{\Pi_{\Delta,t}}\frac{\eta_{t-1}\|\nabla f(w_{t})\|^{2}}{\sqrt{\Sigma_{v_{t-1}}+\mu}}<+\infty\ \ \text{a.s.}\]
nodes.statement_short: The weighted sum is finite a.s.

nodes.name: First result
nodes.statement:
Then, by combining the almost surely boundedness of $\sup_{t\ge 1}\Pi^{-1}_{\Delta,t}$ and ${\sup_{t\ge 1}\Sigma_{v_{t}}}$ from Lemma ef{bounded_moment} and Lemma ef{lem_v_t}, it follows  egin{align*} \sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\eta_{t}\|
abla f(w_{t})\|^{2}&\le \|
abla f(w_{1})\|^{2}+\sum_{t=2}^{+\infty}\eta_{t-1}\|
abla f(w_{t})\|^{2}\&<\|
abla f(w_{1})\|^{2}+\Big(\sup_{t\ge 1}\Pi^{-3/2}_{\Delta,t+1}\Big)\cdot\Big(\sqrt{\sup_{t\ge 1}\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Sigma_{v_{t}}}+\mu\Big)\cdot\sum_{t=2}^{+\infty}\Pi_{\Delta,t} rac{\eta_{t-1}\|
abla f(w_{t})\|^{2}}{\sqrt{\Sigma_{v_{t-1}}}+\mu}\&<+\infty\ \ 	ext{	ext{a.s.}} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Remove the weights using Lemmas C.1 and C.9

nodes.name: Transfer to u_t
nodes.statement:
According to the L-smoothness assumption (Assumption ef{ass_2}), it is immediate that \[ |\|
abla f(w_{t})\| - \|
abla f(u_{t})\| |\leq L_{f} \|w_{t} - u_{t}\| =  rac{L_{f}  eta_{1}}{1 -  eta_{1}} \|\eta_{v_{t-1}} \circ m_{t-1}\|,\] that is,  egin{align*} \|
abla f(u_{t})\|^{2}&\le\left(\|
abla f(w_{t})\|+ rac{L_{f}  eta_{1}}{1 -  eta_{1}} \|\eta_{v_{t-1}} \circ m_{t-1}\|ight)^{2}\&\le 2\|
abla f(w_{t})\|^{2}+ rac{2L_{f}^{2} eta_{1}^{2}}{(1- eta_{1})^{2}} \|\eta_{v_{t-1}} \circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}. \end{align*} This implies  egin{align*} \sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\eta_{t}\|
abla f(u_{t})\|^{2}&\le 2\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\eta_{t}\|
abla f(w_{t})\|^{2}+ rac{2L_{f}^{2} eta_{1}^{2}}{(1- eta_{1})^{2}} \sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\|\eta_{v_{t-1}} \circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Compare gradients at w_t and u_t

nodes.name: Momentum energy
nodes.statement: According to Property \ref{property_2}, for any \(\delta > 0\), \begin{align*} \left(\frac{L_{f} \beta_{1}}{1 - \beta_{1}} \right)^{2}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\|\eta_{v_{t-1}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}&\le \mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\|\eta_{v_{t}}\circ g_{t}\|^{2}\right)+\mathcal{O}(1)\\&\mathop{\le}^{\text{Eq. \ref{Gamma}}}\mathcal{O}(1). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expected momentum energy is O(1) by Eq. Gamma

nodes.name: Remaining results
nodes.statement: Applying the \emph{Lebesgue's Monotone Convergence theorem}, we obtain \begin{align} \left(\frac{L_{f} \beta_{1}}{1 - \beta_{1}} \right)^{2}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\eta_{v_{t-1}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2} <+\infty\ \ \text{a.s.,} \end{align} that is \begin{align*} \sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\eta_{t}\|\nabla f(u_{t})\|^{2}&\le 2\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\eta_{t}\|\nabla f(w_{t})\|^{2}+\frac{2L_{f}^{2}\beta_{1}^{2}}{(1-\beta_{1})^{2}} \sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\|\eta_{v_{t-1}} \circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}<+\infty\ \ \text{a.s..} \tag*{\qedhere} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Monotone convergence gives the last two results

nodes.name: Lemma C.5
nodes.statement: According to Lemma \ref{lem_sum}, we have: \begin{align*} \sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\zeta_{i}(t)\bigg]\le\begin{cases} C_{4,\delta}, & \text{if } \delta\in(0,1/2) \\ C_{5}+C_{6}\mathbb{E}\left[\ln(S_{T})\right], & \text{if } \delta = 0\end{cases}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the weighted descent sum

nodes.name: Monotonicity
nodes.statement: According to the monotonicity of $\eta_{v_{t},i}$ in Property \ref{property_0} and the monotonicity of $\Pi_{\Delta,t}$ itself, we obtain the following inequality. \begin{align*} \sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\Pi_{\Delta,T}\frac{\|\nabla f(w_{t})\|^{2}}{T^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}(\sqrt{v_{T}}+\mu)}\bigg]\le \sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\Pi_{\Delta,T}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\zeta_{i}(t)\bigg]\le\begin{cases} C_{4,\delta}, & \text{if } \delta\in(0,1/2) \\ C_{5}+C_{6}\mathbb{E}\left[\ln(S_{T})\right], & \text{if } \delta = 0\end{cases}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound zeta terms with the final step size

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement:
For the leftmost part of the above inequality, we apply the \emph{Cauchy-Schwarz inequality} and obtain  egin{align*} \mathbb{E} ig[\Pi_{\Delta,T}^{-1}T^{ rac{1}{2}+\delta}(\sqrt{v_{T}}+\mu) ig]\Bigg( \sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\Bigg[\Pi_{\Delta,T} rac{\|
abla f(w_{t})\|^{2}}{T^{ rac{1}{2}+\delta}(\sqrt{v_{T}}+\mu)} igg]\Bigg) \ge \mathbb{E}\left[\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|
abla f(w_{t})\|^{2}}ight], \end{align*} which means  egin{align*} \mathbb{E}\left[\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|
abla f(w_{t})\|^{2}}ight] \le  egin{cases} C_{4,\delta}\mathbb{E} ig[\Pi_{\Delta,T}^{-1}T^{ rac{1}{2}+\delta}(\sqrt{v_{T}}+\mu) ig], & 	ext{if } \delta\in(0,1/2) \ C_{5}\mathbb{E} ig[\Pi_{\Delta,T}^{-1}T^{ rac{1}{2}+\delta}(\sqrt{v_{T}}+\mu) ig]+C_{6}\mathbb{E} ig[\Pi_{\Delta,T}^{-1}T^{ rac{1}{2}+\delta}(\sqrt{v_{T}}+\mu) ig]\mathbb{E}\left[\ln(S_{T})ight], & 	ext{if } \delta = 0\end{cases}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz bounds E sqrt(sum ||grad||^2)

nodes.name: Lemmas C.8, C.9, C.1
nodes.statement: Combining the results from Lemma \ref{lem_S_T}, Lemma \ref{lem_v_t} and Lemma \ref{bounded_moment}, we obtain \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\big[\Pi_{\Delta,T}^{-1}T^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}(\sqrt{v_{T}}+\mu)\big]&\le 2T^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[\Pi^{-3}_{\Delta,T}] }\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,T}(v_{T}+\mu^{2})]}\\&\le \begin{cases} C^{1/2}_{v,d,3}\mathcal{O}(T^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}), & \text{if } \gamma>1 \\ C^{1/2}_{v,d,3}\mathcal{O}({T}^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}), & \text{if } \gamma=1,\ \delta \in(0,1]\\ C^{1/2}_{v,d,3}\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T}\ln T), & \text{if } \gamma=1,\ \delta=0.\end{cases} \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[\ln(S_{T})]=\frac{4}{3}\mathbb{E}[\ln(S^{3/4}_{T})]\le \frac{4}{3}\ln(\mathbb{E}[S^{3/4}_{T}])=\begin{cases} \mathcal{O}(\ln T), & \text{if } \delta\in(0,1/2) \\ \mathcal{O}(\ln T)+\mathcal{O}(\ln\ln T), & \text{if } \delta = 0\end{cases}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the weight factor and E[ln S_T]

nodes.name: Rate in expectation
nodes.statement: Combining the two estimates above, we finally obtain \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\left[\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\nabla f(w_{t})\|^{2}}\right]\le \begin{cases} \mathcal{O}(T^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}), & \text{if }\delta\in(0,1/2) \\ \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T}\ln T), & \text{if } \gamma>1,\ \ \delta = 0\\ \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T}\ln^{2} T), & \text{if } \gamma=1,\ \ \delta = 0.\end{cases} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: E sqrt(sum ||grad||^2) bound

nodes.name: High probability
nodes.statement: This implies that for any \( s \in (0,1) \), the inequality \begin{align*} \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|\nabla f(w_{t})\|^{2}\le \begin{cases} \mathcal{O}\Big(\frac{1}{s^2}\frac{1}{T^{\frac{1}{2}-\delta}}\Big), & \text{if }\delta\in(0,1/2) \\ \mathcal{O}\Big(\frac{1}{s^2}\frac{\ln T}{\sqrt{T}}\Big), & \text{if } \gamma>1,\ \ \delta = 0\\ \mathcal{O}\Big(\frac{1}{s^2}\frac{\ln^{2} T}{\sqrt{T}}\Big), & \text{if } \gamma=1,\ \ \delta = 0\end{cases} \tag*{\qedhere} \end{align*} holds with probability at least \( 1 - s \).
nodes.statement_short: Markov's inequality gives the probability-1-s bound

nodes.name: Use Eq. (sqrt)
nodes.statement: From Eq. \eqref{sqrt}, we have $\forall\ t_{0}\ge 0,$ \[ \lim_{T\rightarrow+\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\inf_{t_0< t\le T}\|\nabla f(w_{t})\|\right] \le \lim_{T\rightarrow+\infty}\frac{1}{T-t_0+1}\mathbb{E}\left[\sqrt{\sum_{t=t_0}^{T}\|\nabla f(w_{t})\|^{2}}\right]=0. \]
nodes.statement_short: Expected infimum over a window tends to zero

nodes.name: Monotone convergence
nodes.statement:
Since, for a fixed \( t_0 \), the sequence \( \left\{ \inf_{t_0 < t \leq T} \|f(w_t)\| ight\}_{T > t_0} \) is monotonically decreasing and non-negative, by the \emph{Lebesgue's Monotone Convergence theorem}, we readily obtain:  egin{align*} \mathbb{E}\left[\inf_{t>t_{0}}\|
abla f(w_{t})\|ight]= \mathbb{E}\left[\lim_{Tightarrow+\infty}\inf_{t_{0}<t\le T}\|
abla f(w_{t})\|ight]=\lim_{Tightarrow+\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\inf_{t_{0}<t\le T}\|
abla f(w_{t})\|ight]=0 \end{align*} The second equality follows from the \emph{Lebesgue's Monotone Convergence theorem}, which allows the interchange of the limit and expectation.
nodes.statement_short: Interchange limit and expectation

nodes.name: Zero infimum a.s.
nodes.statement:
Since \(\inf_{t > t_0} \|
abla f(w_t)\| \geq 0\), we can directly deduce that \(\inf_{t > t_0} \|
abla f(w_t)\| = 0\ \ 	ext{a.s.},\) from the fact that \(\mathbb{E}\left[\inf_{t > t_0} \|
abla f(w_t)\|ight] = 0.\)
nodes.statement_short: Nonnegative with zero mean, so zero a.s.

nodes.name: Subsequence
nodes.statement: Furthermore, given the arbitrariness of \( t_0 \), we can obtain that there exists a subsequence \( \{w_{c_{t}}\}_{t \ge 1} \) of \( \{w_{t}\}_{t \ge 1} \) such that \[ \lim_{t \rightarrow +\infty} \|\nabla f(w_{c_{t}})\| = 0 \quad \text{a.s.} \] This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Extract an a.s. convergent subsequence

nodes.name: Reduce to u_t
nodes.statement:
According to Lemma ef{lem_sum_1}, we have \[|\|
abla f(w_{t})\| - \|
abla f(u_{t})\| |\leq L_{f} \|w_{t} - u_{t}\| =  rac{L_{f}  eta_{1}}{1 -  eta_{1}} \|\eta_{v_{t-1}} \circ m_{t-1}\|ightarrow 0\ \ 	ext{a.s.}\] This implies that we only need to prove $\lim_{t ightarrow +\infty} \|
abla f(u_{t})\| = 0 \ \ 	ext{a.s.}$ To achieve this objective, we proceed as follows.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma C.10 shows ||grad f(w_t)|| - ||grad f(u_t)|| -> 0, so it suffices to treat u_t

nodes.name: Crossing stopping times
nodes.statement:
For any $l > 0$, we construct the following stopping time ootnote{In this paper, we adopt the following definition of stopping time: Let $	au$ be a random variable defined on the filtered probability space $(\Omega, \mathscr{F}, (\mathscr{F}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}, \mathbb{P})$ with values in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{+\infty\}$. Then $	au$ is called a {stopping time} (with respect to the filtration $ (\mathscr{F}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$) if the condition \( \{	au = n\} \in \mathscr{F}_n \) holds for all $n$.} sequence $\{	au_{l,n}\}_{n \geq 1}:$  egin{align*} &	au_{l,1}:=\min\{t\ge 1:\|
abla f(u_{t})\|>l\},\ \ 	au_{l,2}:=\min\{t>	au_{l,1}:\|
abla f(u_{t})\|\le l\},\&...,\&	au_{l,2k-1}:=\min\{t>	au_{l,2k-2}:\|
abla f(u_{t})\|>l\},\ \ 	au_{l,2k}:=\min\{t>	au_{l,2k-1}:\|
abla f(u_{t})\|\le l\}. \end{align*} According to the subsequence convergence result in Lemma ef{sub}, we know that when $	au_{2k-1} < +\infty \ ( orall\ k \geq 1)$, it must hold that $	au_{2k} < +\infty \ \ 	ext{a.s.}$ We now discuss two cases.
nodes.statement_short: Define up/down crossing times of level l; Lemma C.6 gives finiteness

nodes.name: Case 1: finitely many crossings
nodes.statement: 1. When there exists some $k_{0} \geq 1$ such that $\tau_{2k_{0}-1} = +\infty$, this implies that eventually $\{\|\nabla f(u_{t})\|\}_{t \geq 1}$ will remain below $l$, i.e., \begin{align} \limsup_{t \rightarrow +\infty} \|\nabla f(u_{t})\| < l. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Gradient eventually stays below l

nodes.name: Case 2: infinitely many crossings
nodes.statement:
2. Next, we focus on the second case, where for all $	au_{2k-1}$, we have $	au_{2k-1} < +\infty$. In this situation, we examine the behavior of $\sup_{	au_{2k-1} \leq t < 	au_{2k}} \|
abla f(u_{t})\|.$ We have  egin{align*} \sup_{	au_{2k-1} \leq t < 	au_{2k}} \|
abla f(u_{t})\|&\le l+\sup_{	au_{2k-1} \leq t < 	au_{2k}} \|
abla f(u_{t})\|-\|
abla f(u_{	au_{2k-1}-1})\|\&\le l+\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1} ig|\|
abla f(u_{t})\|-\|
abla f(u_{t-1})\| ig|\Bigg) \&\mathop{\le}^{	ext{l-smooth}}l+\Bigg( L_{f}\sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\|u_{t}-u_{t-1}\|\Bigg) \&\mathop{\le}^{	ext{Eq. ef{u_{t}}}}l+L_{f}\underbrace{\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\|\eta_{v_{t}}\circ g_{t}\|\Bigg)}_{\Upsilon_{k,1}}\&+  rac{ eta_{1}L^{2}_{f}}{1- eta_{1}}\underbrace{\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\|\Delta_{t}\circ m_{t-1}\|\Bigg)}_{\Upsilon_{k,2}}. \end{align*} Our next goal is to prove separately that $\limsup_{k ightarrow +\infty} \Upsilon_{k,1} = 0 \ \ 	ext{a.s.}$ and $\limsup_{k ightarrow +\infty} \Upsilon_{k,2} = 0 \ \ 	ext{a.s.}$ For $\Upsilon_{k,1}$, we have  egin{align*} \Upsilon_{k,1}&=\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\|\eta_{v_{t}}\circ g_{t}\|\Bigg)=\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}|g_{t,i}|\Bigg)\&=\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d} rac{\eta_{t}|g_{t,i}|}{\sqrt{v_{t}}+\mu}\Bigg)\le \Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d} rac{\eta_{t}|g_{t,i}|}{\mu}\Bigg)\&= rac{1}{\mu}\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}{\eta_{t}\mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}||\mathscr{F}_{t-1}]}\Bigg)\&+ rac{1}{\mu}\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}{\eta_{t}(|g_{t,i}|-\mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}||\mathscr{F}_{t-1}])}\Bigg)\&= rac{1}{\mu}\underbrace{\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\eta_{t}{\mathbb{E}[|g_{t}||\mathscr{F}_{t-1}]}\Bigg)}_{\Upsilon_{k,1,1}}+ rac{1}{\mu}\underbrace{\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}{\eta_{t}(|g_{t,i}|-\mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}||\mathscr{F}_{t-1}])}\Bigg)}_{\Upsilon_{k,1,2}}. \end{align*} For $\Upsilon_{k,1,1},$ we have  egin{align*} \Upsilon_{k,1,1}&\mathop{\le}^{	ext{Property ef{property_-1}}} \Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\eta_{t} ig((A+2L_{f}B)(f(w_{t})-f^{*})+C ig)\Bigg)\&\le  ig((A+2L_{f}B)\sup_{t\ge 1}(f(w_{t})-f^{*})+C ig)\cdot\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\eta_{t}\Bigg)\&= ig((A+2L_{f}B)\sup_{t\ge 1}(f(w_{t})-f^{*})+C ig)\cdot\Bigg(\eta_{	au_{2k-1}}+\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}}\eta_{t}\Bigg)\Bigg)\&\mathop{\le}^{(a)} rac{1}{l^{2}} ig((A+2L_{f}B)\sup_{t\ge 1}(f(w_{t})-f^{*})+C ig)\cdot\Bigg(\eta_{	au_{2k-1}}+\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}}^{	au_{2k}-1}\eta_{t}\|
abla f(u_{t})\|^{2}\Bigg)\Bigg). \end{align*} In step $(a)$, this is due to the fact that, over the interval $[	au_{2k-1}, 	au_{2k})$, we always have $\|
abla f(u_{t})\|^{2} > l^{2}$. Based on Lemma ef{lem_sum_1}, we know that \[\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\eta_{t}\|
abla f(u_{t})\|^{2} < +\infty \quad 	ext{a.s.}\] By applying the \emph{Cauchy's} convergence principle, we can prove that \[\lim_{kightarrow+\infty} \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}}^{	au_{2k}-1}\eta_{t}\|
abla f(u_{t})\|^{2}= 0 \quad 	ext{a.s.}\] On the other hand, it is evident that $\lim_{kightarrow+\infty}{\eta_{	au_{2k-1}}}= 0.$ Meanwhile, based on Lemma ef{lem_g} and Lemma ef{bounded_moment}, we have \[\sup_{t \geq 1} (f(w_{t}) - f^*) \leq \Big( \sup_{t \geq 1} \Pi_{\Delta,t}^{-1} \Big) \cdot \Big( \sup_{t \geq 1}  ig(\Pi_{\Delta,t+1} (f(w_{t}) - f^*)  ig)\Big) < +\infty \quad 	ext{a.s.}\] Therefore, \[\limsup_{k 	o +\infty} \Upsilon_{k,1,1} = \lim_{k 	o +\infty} \Upsilon_{k,1,1} = 0.\] For $\Upsilon_{k,1,2}$, we consider the following martingale $\{(\overline{X}_{T},\mathscr{F}_{T})\}_{T\ge 1},$ where \[\overline{X}_{T}:=\sum_{t=1}^{T} \sum_{i=1}^{d} \eta_{t} (|g_{t,i}| - \mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}| \mid \mathscr{F}_{t-1}]).\] We can compute  egin{align*} &\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty} \mathbb{E}\Bigg[\left( \sum_{i=1}^{d} \eta_{t} (|g_{t,i}| - \mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}| \mid \mathscr{F}_{t-1}]) ight)^{2} igg|\mathscr{F}_{t-1}\Bigg]\le d\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\eta^{2}_{t}\sum_{i=1}^{d} \mathbb{E}[(|g_{t,i}| - \mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}| \mid \mathscr{F}_{t-1}])^{2} ]\ \le& d\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\eta^{2}_{t}\sum_{i=1}^{d} \mathbb{E}[\|g_{t}\|^{2} \mid \mathscr{F}_{t-1}] \ \mathop{\le}^{	ext{Property ef{property_-1}}}& d\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\eta^{2}_{t}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Big( (A+2L_{f}B)\sup_{t\ge 1}(f(w_{t})-f^*)+C\Big)\ \le & d\sum_{i=1}^{d} igg( (A+2L_{f}B)\Big(\sup_{t\ge 1}\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Big)\Big(\sup_{t\ge 1}(f(w_{t})-f^*)+C\Big) igg)\cdot\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\eta^{2}_{t}\\mathop{<}^{	ext{Lemma ef{bounded_moment} and ef{lem_g}}} & +\infty\ \ 	ext{a.s.} \end{align*} By the \emph{Martingale Convergence} theorem, we obtain \[\lim_{T 	o +\infty} \overline{X}_{T} = \sum_{t=1}^{+\infty} \sum_{i=1}^{d} \eta_{t} (|g_{t,i}| - \mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}| \mid \mathscr{F}_{t-1}]) < +\infty\ \ 	ext{a.s.}\] Using the \emph{Cauchy's Convergence} principle, we prove that \[\limsup_{k 	o +\infty} \Upsilon_{k,1,2} = \lim_{kightarrow+\infty}\sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}{\eta_{t}(|g_{t,i}|-\mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}||\mathscr{F}_{t-1}])} = 0 \quad 	ext{a.s.}\] Combining the above two limit proofs for $\Upsilon_{t,1,1}$ and $\Upsilon_{t,1,2}$, we conclude that \[\limsup_{k 	o +\infty} \Upsilon_{t,1} = 0 \quad 	ext{a.s.}\] Similarly, it can be shown that $\lim_{k 	o +\infty} \Upsilon_{k,2} = 0 \ 	ext{a.s.}$ Combining the limit results for $\Upsilon_{k,1}$ and $\Upsilon_{k,2}$, we conclude that \[\limsup_{k 	o +\infty} \sup_{	au_{2k-1} \leq t < 	au_{2k}} \|
abla f(u_{t})\|\leq l + 0 = l.\]
nodes.statement_short: Excursion increments vanish

nodes.name: Excursion bound
nodes.statement:
2. Next, we focus on the second case, where for all $	au_{2k-1}$, we have $	au_{2k-1} < +\infty$. In this situation, we examine the behavior of $\sup_{	au_{2k-1} \leq t < 	au_{2k}} \|
abla f(u_{t})\|.$ We have  egin{align*} \sup_{	au_{2k-1} \leq t < 	au_{2k}} \|
abla f(u_{t})\|&\le l+\sup_{	au_{2k-1} \leq t < 	au_{2k}} \|
abla f(u_{t})\|-\|
abla f(u_{	au_{2k-1}-1})\|\&\le l+\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1} ig|\|
abla f(u_{t})\|-\|
abla f(u_{t-1})\| ig|\Bigg) \&\mathop{\le}^{	ext{l-smooth}}l+\Bigg( L_{f}\sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\|u_{t}-u_{t-1}\|\Bigg) \&\mathop{\le}^{	ext{Eq. ef{u_{t}}}}l+L_{f}\underbrace{\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\|\eta_{v_{t}}\circ g_{t}\|\Bigg)}_{\Upsilon_{k,1}}\&+  rac{ eta_{1}L^{2}_{f}}{1- eta_{1}}\underbrace{\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\|\Delta_{t}\circ m_{t-1}\|\Bigg)}_{\Upsilon_{k,2}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the excursion by l plus Upsilon_{k,1} and Upsilon_{k,2}

nodes.name: Split Upsilon_{k,1}
nodes.statement: Our next goal is to prove separately that $\limsup_{k \rightarrow +\infty} \Upsilon_{k,1} = 0 \ \ \text{a.s.}$ and $\limsup_{k \rightarrow +\infty} \Upsilon_{k,2} = 0 \ \ \text{a.s.}$ For $\Upsilon_{k,1}$, we have \begin{align*} \Upsilon_{k,1}&=\Bigg( \sum_{t=\tau_{2k-1}-1}^{\tau_{2k}-1}\|\eta_{v_{t}}\circ g_{t}\|\Bigg)=\Bigg( \sum_{t=\tau_{2k-1}-1}^{\tau_{2k}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}|g_{t,i}|\Bigg)\\&=\Bigg( \sum_{t=\tau_{2k-1}-1}^{\tau_{2k}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\frac{\eta_{t}|g_{t,i}|}{\sqrt{v_{t}}+\mu}\Bigg)\le \Bigg( \sum_{t=\tau_{2k-1}-1}^{\tau_{2k}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\frac{\eta_{t}|g_{t,i}|}{\mu}\Bigg)\\&=\frac{1}{\mu}\Bigg( \sum_{t=\tau_{2k-1}-1}^{\tau_{2k}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}{\eta_{t}\mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}||\mathscr{F}_{t-1}]}\Bigg)\\&+\frac{1}{\mu}\Bigg( \sum_{t=\tau_{2k-1}-1}^{\tau_{2k}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}{\eta_{t}(|g_{t,i}|-\mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}||\mathscr{F}_{t-1}])}\Bigg)\\&=\frac{1}{\mu}\underbrace{\Bigg( \sum_{t=\tau_{2k-1}-1}^{\tau_{2k}-1}\eta_{t}{\mathbb{E}[|g_{t}||\mathscr{F}_{t-1}]}\Bigg)}_{\Upsilon_{k,1,1}}+\frac{1}{\mu}\underbrace{\Bigg( \sum_{t=\tau_{2k-1}-1}^{\tau_{2k}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}{\eta_{t}(|g_{t,i}|-\mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}||\mathscr{F}_{t-1}])}\Bigg)}_{\Upsilon_{k,1,2}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split Upsilon_{k,1} into predictable and martingale parts

nodes.name: Bound Upsilon_{k,1,1}
nodes.statement:
For $\Upsilon_{k,1,1},$ we have  egin{align*} \Upsilon_{k,1,1}&\mathop{\le}^{	ext{Property ef{property_-1}}} \Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\eta_{t} ig((A+2L_{f}B)(f(w_{t})-f^{*})+C ig)\Bigg)\&\le  ig((A+2L_{f}B)\sup_{t\ge 1}(f(w_{t})-f^{*})+C ig)\cdot\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}-1}\eta_{t}\Bigg)\&= ig((A+2L_{f}B)\sup_{t\ge 1}(f(w_{t})-f^{*})+C ig)\cdot\Bigg(\eta_{	au_{2k-1}}+\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}-1}^{	au_{2k}}\eta_{t}\Bigg)\Bigg)\&\mathop{\le}^{(a)} rac{1}{l^{2}} ig((A+2L_{f}B)\sup_{t\ge 1}(f(w_{t})-f^{*})+C ig)\cdot\Bigg(\eta_{	au_{2k-1}}+\Bigg( \sum_{t=	au_{2k-1}}^{	au_{2k}-1}\eta_{t}\|
abla f(u_{t})\|^{2}\Bigg)\Bigg). \end{align*} In step $(a)$, this is due to the fact that, over the interval $[	au_{2k-1}, 	au_{2k})$, we always have $\|
abla f(u_{t})\|^{2} > l^{2}$. Based on Lemma ef{lem_sum_1}, we know that \[\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\eta_{t}\|
abla f(u_{t})\|^{2} < +\infty \quad 	ext{a.s.}\]
nodes.statement_short: Use Property 1 and the level-crossing condition

nodes.name: Upsilon_{k,1,1} -> 0
nodes.statement: By applying the \emph{Cauchy's} convergence principle, we can prove that \[\lim_{k\rightarrow+\infty} \sum_{t=\tau_{2k-1}}^{\tau_{2k}-1}\eta_{t}\|\nabla f(u_{t})\|^{2}= 0 \quad \text{a.s.}\] On the other hand, it is evident that $\lim_{k\rightarrow+\infty}{\eta_{\tau_{2k-1}}}= 0.$ Meanwhile, based on Lemma \ref{lem_g} and Lemma \ref{bounded_moment}, we have \[\sup_{t \geq 1} (f(w_{t}) - f^*) \leq \Big( \sup_{t \geq 1} \Pi_{\Delta,t}^{-1} \Big) \cdot \Big( \sup_{t \geq 1} \big(\Pi_{\Delta,t+1} (f(w_{t}) - f^*) \big)\Big) < +\infty \quad \text{a.s.}\] Therefore, \[\limsup_{k \to +\infty} \Upsilon_{k,1,1} = \lim_{k \to +\infty} \Upsilon_{k,1,1} = 0.\]
nodes.statement_short: Lemma C.10, Cauchy criterion, Lemmas C.7 and C.1

nodes.name: Martingale X-bar
nodes.statement: For $\Upsilon_{k,1,2}$, we consider the following martingale $\{(\overline{X}_{T},\mathscr{F}_{T})\}_{T\ge 1},$ where \[\overline{X}_{T}:=\sum_{t=1}^{T} \sum_{i=1}^{d} \eta_{t} (|g_{t,i}| - \mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}| \mid \mathscr{F}_{t-1}]).\] We can compute \begin{align*} &\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty} \mathbb{E}\Bigg[\left( \sum_{i=1}^{d} \eta_{t} (|g_{t,i}| - \mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}| \mid \mathscr{F}_{t-1}]) \right)^{2}\bigg|\mathscr{F}_{t-1}\Bigg]\le d\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\eta^{2}_{t}\sum_{i=1}^{d} \mathbb{E}[(|g_{t,i}| - \mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}| \mid \mathscr{F}_{t-1}])^{2} ]\\ \le& d\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\eta^{2}_{t}\sum_{i=1}^{d} \mathbb{E}[\|g_{t}\|^{2} \mid \mathscr{F}_{t-1}] \\ \mathop{\le}^{\text{Property \ref{property_-1}}}& d\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\eta^{2}_{t}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Big( (A+2L_{f}B)\sup_{t\ge 1}(f(w_{t})-f^*)+C\Big)\\ \le & d\sum_{i=1}^{d}\bigg( (A+2L_{f}B)\Big(\sup_{t\ge 1}\Pi_{\Delta,t}\Big)\Big(\sup_{t\ge 1}(f(w_{t})-f^*)+C\Big)\bigg)\cdot\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\eta^{2}_{t}\\\mathop{<}^{\text{Lemma \ref{bounded_moment} and \ref{lem_g}}} & +\infty\ \ \text{a.s.} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Square-summable martingale increments

nodes.name: Upsilon_{k,1,2} -> 0
nodes.statement: By the \emph{Martingale Convergence} theorem, we obtain \[\lim_{T \to +\infty} \overline{X}_{T} = \sum_{t=1}^{+\infty} \sum_{i=1}^{d} \eta_{t} (|g_{t,i}| - \mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}| \mid \mathscr{F}_{t-1}]) < +\infty\ \ \text{a.s.}\] Using the \emph{Cauchy's Convergence} principle, we prove that \[\limsup_{k \to +\infty} \Upsilon_{k,1,2} = \lim_{k\rightarrow+\infty}\sum_{t=\tau_{2k-1}-1}^{\tau_{2k}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}{\eta_{t}(|g_{t,i}|-\mathbb{E}[|g_{t,i}||\mathscr{F}_{t-1}])} = 0 \quad \text{a.s.}\] Combining the above two limit proofs for $\Upsilon_{t,1,1}$ and $\Upsilon_{t,1,2}$, we conclude that \[\limsup_{k \to +\infty} \Upsilon_{t,1} = 0 \quad \text{a.s.}\] Similarly, it can be shown that $\lim_{k \to +\infty} \Upsilon_{k,2} = 0 \ \text{a.s.}$
nodes.statement_short: Martingale convergence and Cauchy criterion; similarly for Upsilon_{k,2}

nodes.name: Excursion limit
nodes.statement: Combining the limit results for $\Upsilon_{k,1}$ and $\Upsilon_{k,2}$, we conclude that \[\limsup_{k \to +\infty} \sup_{\tau_{2k-1} \leq t < \tau_{2k}} \|\nabla f(u_{t})\|\leq l + 0 = l.\]
nodes.statement_short: limsup of the excursion sup is at most l

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement:
Moreover, combining $\sup_{	au_{2k} \leq t < 	au_{2k+1}} \|
abla f(u_{t})\| < l,$ we can deduce that \[\limsup_{t 	o +\infty} \|
abla f(u_{t})\| \leq l \quad 	ext{a.s.}\] Then, due to the arbitrariness of $l$, we conclude that \[\limsup_{t 	o +\infty} \|
abla f(u_{t})\| = 0 \quad 	ext{a.s.}\] This implies that \[\lim_{t 	o +\infty} \|
abla f(u_{t})\| = 0 \quad 	ext{a.s.}	ag*{\qedhere}\]
nodes.statement_short: limsup <= l for every l, hence the limit is zero

nodes.name: Reduce to expected supremum
nodes.statement:
Since we have already proved the almost sure convergence in Theorem ef{thm:almost_sure}, it is natural to attempt to prove $L_1$ convergence via the \emph{Lebesgue's Dominated Convergence} theorem. To achieve this, we need to find a function $h$ that is $\mathscr{F}_{\infty}$-measurable and satisfies $\mathbb{E}|h| < +\infty$, and such that for all $t \geq 1$, we have $\|
abla f(w_{t})\| \leq |h|.$ Since for all $t,$ we naturally have $\|
abla f(w_{t})\| \leq \sup_{k \geq 1} \|
abla f(w_{k})\|,$ we only need to prove that $\mathbb{E}[\sup_{k \geq 1} \|
abla f(w_{k})\|] < +\infty.$ We proceed to achieve this goal in the rest of the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Dominated convergence: suffices E[sup ||grad f(w_k)||] < infinity

nodes.name: Recall Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: Recall the \emph{Approximate Descent Inequality} (Lemma \ref{sufficient:decrease}). We have \begin{align} \Pi_{\Delta,t}\hat{f}(u_{t+1})-\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})\le& -\frac{1}{2}\Pi_{\Delta,t}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\zeta_{i}(t)\notag+C_{2}\|{\eta_{v_{t-1}}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}+\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}|\nabla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|\\&\ +(L_{f}+1)\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}+\Pi_{\Delta,t}M_{t}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Recall the approximate descent inequality

nodes.name: Hitting time
nodes.statement: For any $\lambda > 0$, define the stopping time $\tau_{\lambda}$ as the first time the sequence $\{\Pi_{\Delta,t} \hat{f}(u_{t})\}_{t \geq 1}$ exceeds $\lambda$, i.e., \[\tau_{\lambda} := \min\{t \geq 2 : \Pi_{\Delta,t} \hat{f}(u_{t}) > \lambda\}.\] It can be rigorously verified that $\tau_{\lambda}$ is a stopping time with respect to the filtration $\{\mathscr{F}_{t}\}_{t \geq 1}$, and satisfies a special property $[\tau_{\lambda} = n] \in \mathscr{F}_{n-1}$ for all $n \geq 1$. This implies that the preceding time $\tau_{\lambda} - 1$ is also a stopping time.
nodes.statement_short: First time Pi f-hat exceeds lambda

nodes.name: Stopped sum
nodes.statement: Next, for any deterministic time $T \geq 3$, we define $\tau_{\lambda,T} := \tau_{\lambda} \wedge T$. We then sum the indices of Equation (\ref{adam_16.01}) from $1$ to $\tau_{\lambda,T} - 1$. Specifically, we have \begin{align*} \Pi_{\Delta,\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\hat{f}(u_{\tau_{\lambda,T}})\le& \Pi_{\Delta,0}\hat{f}(u_{1})+C_{2}\sum_{t=1}^{\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\|{\eta_{v_{t-1}}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}+\sum_{t=1}^{\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}|\nabla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|\\&\ +(L_{f}+1)\sum_{t=1}^{\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}+\sum_{t=1}^{\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\Pi_{\Delta,t}M_{t}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Sum the descent inequality up to the stopped time

nodes.name: Expectation
nodes.statement: Taking the expectation on both sides, we obtain \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\Big[\Pi_{\Delta,\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\hat{f}(u_{\tau_{\lambda,T}})\Big]\le & \mathbb{E}\Big[\Pi_{\Delta,0}\hat{f}(u_{1})\Big]+C_{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\|{\eta_{v_{t-1}}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}\right]\\&\ +\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}|\nabla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|\right]+(L_{f}+1)\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}\right]\\&\ +\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\Pi_{\Delta,t}M_{t}\right]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Take expectations

nodes.name: Optional stopping
nodes.statement: Since $\{\Pi_{\Delta,t}M_{t}, \mathscr{F}_{t}\}_{t \geq 1}$ is a martingale difference sequence and $\tau_{\lambda,T} \le T<+\infty$, by \emph{Doob's Stopped} theorem, we know that \[\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\Pi_{\Delta,t}M_{t}\right]=0.\] This implies \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\Big[\Pi_{\Delta,\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\hat{f}(u_{\tau_{\lambda,T}})\Big]&\le \mathbb{E}\Big[\Pi_{\Delta,0}\hat{f}(u_{1})\Big]+C_{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\|{\eta_{v_{t-1}}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}\right]\\&+\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}|\nabla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|\right]+(L_{f}+1)\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}\right]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The stopped martingale term has zero mean

nodes.name: Uniform bound M-bar
nodes.statement:
Using Property ef{property_2} and Lemma ef{lem_sum'}, we obtain  egin{align*} &C_{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{	au_{\lambda,T}-1}\|{\eta_{v_{t-1}}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}ight]+\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{	au_{\lambda,T}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}|
abla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|ight]\&+(L_{f}+1)\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{	au_{\lambda,T}-1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}ight]\ \le& C_{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|{\eta_{v_{t-1}}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}ight]+\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}|
abla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|ight]\&+(L_{f}+1)\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}ight] \= & \mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\left[\|\eta_{v_{t}}\circ g_{t}\|^{2}ight]ight)+\mathcal{O}(1)\\mathop{=}^{	ext{Eq. ef{Gamma}}} &\mathcal{O}(1). \end{align*} This means \[\mathbb{E}\Big[\Pi_{\Delta,	au_{\lambda,T}-1}\hat{f}(u_{	au_{\lambda,T}})\Big]\le \overline{M}<+\infty,\] where  egin{align*} \overline{M}&:=C_{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\|{\eta_{v_{t-1}}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}ight]+\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Delta_{t,i}|
abla_{i} f(u_{t})m_{t-1,i}|ight]\&+(L_{f}+1)\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{+\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{d}\eta_{v_{t},i}^{2}g_{t,i}^{2}ight]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Error sums bounded by a constant

nodes.name: Maximal inequality
nodes.statement: Meanwhile, we observe the following event decomposition \[\Big[\sup_{2\le t<T}\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})>\lambda\Big]=\bigcup_{k=2}^{T-1}[\tau_{\lambda}=k]=\bigcup_{k=2}^{T-1}[\tau_{\lambda,T}=k].\] Moreover, since for any $j \neq k$, we have $[\tau_{\lambda,T} = j] \cap [\tau_{\lambda,T} = k] = \emptyset$, it follows that \begin{align} \mathbb{P}\Big[\sup_{2\le t<T}\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})>\lambda\Big]&=\sum_{k=2}^{T-1}\mathbb{P}[\tau_{\lambda,T}=k]\mathop{\le}^{\text{Markov's inequality}}\frac{1}{\lambda}\sum_{k=2}^{T-1}\mathbb{E}\big[\Pi_{\Delta,k}\hat{f}(u_{k})\mathbb{I}_{[\tau_{\lambda,T}=k]}\big]\notag\\&<\frac{1}{\lambda}\mathbb{E}\Big[\Pi_{\Delta,\tau_{\lambda,T}-1}\hat{f}(u_{\tau_{\lambda,T}})\Big]\le \frac{\overline{M}}{\lambda}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Markov's inequality at the hitting time

nodes.name: Tail integral
nodes.statement: Next, for any $K \geq 1$, we compute $\mathbb{E}\Big[\big(\sup_{2\le t<T}\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})\big)^{3/4} \wedge K\Big].$ We have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\Big[\big(\sup_{2\le t<T}\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})\big)^{3/4} \wedge K\Big]&=-\int_{0}^{+\infty}x\ \ \text{d}\left(\mathbb{P}\left[\left(\sup_{2\le t<T}\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})\right)^{3/4} \wedge K>x\right]\right)\\&=-\int_{0}^{+\infty}\bigg(\int_{0}^{x}1\text{d}\lambda\bigg)\text{d}\left(\mathbb{P}\left[\left(\sup_{2\le t<T}\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})\right)^{3/4} \wedge K>x\right]\right)\\&\mathop{=}^{\text{\emph{Fubini's} theorem}}-\int_{0}^{+\infty}\left(\int_{\lambda}^{+\infty}1\text{d}\left(\mathbb{P}\left[\left(\sup_{2\le t<T}\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})\right)^{3/4} \wedge K>x\right]\right)\right)\text{d}\lambda\\&=\int_{0}^{+\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[\left(\sup_{2\le t<T}\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})\right)^{3/4} \wedge K>\lambda\right]\text{d}\lambda\\&\le 1+\int_{1}^{+\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[\left(\sup_{2\le t<T}\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})\right)^{3/4} \wedge K>\lambda\right]\text{d}\lambda\\&=1+\int_{1}^{+\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[\left(\sup_{2\le t<T}\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})\right) \wedge K^{4/3}>\lambda^{4/3}\right]\text{d}\lambda\\&<1+\int_{1}^{+\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[\left(\sup_{2\le t<T}\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})\right)>\lambda^{4/3}\right]\text{d}\lambda\\&\mathop{<}^{\text{Eq. \ref{max}}}1+\int_{1}^{+\infty}\frac{\overline{M}}{\lambda^{4/3}}\text{d}\lambda\\&=1+3\overline{M}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the tail to bound the 3/4 moment

nodes.name: Monotone convergence
nodes.statement: Next, we take \(K \rightarrow +\infty\) and apply the \emph{Lebesgue's Monotone Convergence} theorem, which yield \[ \mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\sup_{2\le t<T}\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})\Big)^{3/4}\Big]\le 1+3\overline{M}.\] By taking $T \rightarrow +\infty$ and applying the \emph{Lebesgue's Monotone Convergence} theorem once again, we obtain \[\mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\sup_{t\ge 2}\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})\Big)^{3/4}\Big]\le 1+3\overline{M}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Remove truncation and let T -> infinity

nodes.name: Holder
nodes.statement: Note that for any finite $t$, we have $\Pi_{\Delta,t+1} \geq \Pi_{\Delta,\infty}$ (where $\Pi_{\Delta,\infty}$ is defined in Lemma \ref{bounded_moment}). Thus, we have \[\mathbb{E}\Big[\Pi^{3/4}_{\Delta,\infty}\Big(\sup_{t\ge 2}\hat{f}(u_{t})\Big)^{3/4}\Big] \le \mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\sup_{t\ge 2}\Pi_{\Delta,t-1}\hat{f}(u_{t})\Big)^{3/4}\Big]\le 1+3\overline{M}.\] Next, by applying \emph{Hölder's} inequality, we obtain \[ \mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\sup_{t\ge 2}\hat{f}(u_{t})\Big)^{1/2}\Big]\le \mathbb{E}^{1/3}\Big[\Pi^{-3/2}_{\Delta,\infty}\Big]\mathbb{E}^{2/3}\Big[\Pi^{3/4}_{\Delta,\infty}\Big(\sup_{t\ge 2}\hat{f}(u_{t})\Big)^{3/4}\Big]\mathop{\le}^{\text{Lemma \ref{bounded_moment}}}C^{1/3}_{v,d,3/2}(1+3\overline{M})^{2/3}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Remove Pi using Lemma C.1 and Holder

nodes.name: Property 5
nodes.statement: Then, according to Property \ref{property_2}, we can bound ${f}(w_{t})-f^*$ using $\hat{f}(u_{t})$, i.e., \begin{align*} {f}(w_{t})-f^*&\le (L_{f}+1)(f(u_t)-f^*)+\frac{(L_{f}+1)\beta_{1}^{2}}{2(1-\beta_1)^{2}}\|\eta_{v_{t-1}}\circ m_{t-1}\|^{2}+L_{f}f^*\\&\le (L_{f}+1)\hat{f}(u_{t})+\frac{(L_{f}+1)\beta_{1}^{2}}{2\alpha_{1}(1-\beta_1)^{2}}+L_{f}f^*. \end{align*} That means \[\mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\sup_{t\ge 2}\big(f(w_{t})-f^*\big)\Big)^{1/2}\Big]\le \sqrt{L_{f}+1}C^{1/3}_{v,d,3/2}(1+3\overline{M})^{2/3}+\sqrt{\frac{(L_{f}+1)\beta_{1}^{2}}{2\alpha_{1}(1-\beta_1)^{2}}+L_{f}|f^*|}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Pass from f-hat(u_t) to f(w_t)-f*

nodes.name: Lemma B.2
nodes.statement:
Finally, according to Lemma ef{loss_bound}, we obtain  egin{align*} \mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{t\ge 2}\|
abla f(w_{t})\|\Big]&\le \sqrt{2L_{f}}\mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\sup_{t\ge 2} ig(f(w_{t})-f^* ig)\Big)^{1/2}\Big]\&<\sqrt{2L_{f}}\left(\sqrt{L_{f}+1}C^{1/3}_{v,d,3/2}(1+3\overline{M})^{2/3}+\sqrt{ rac{(L_{f}+1) eta_{1}^{2}}{2\alpha_{1}(1- eta_1)^{2}}+L_{f}|f^*|}ight). \end{align*} Adding the first term concludes  egin{align*} \mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{t\ge 1}\|
abla f(w_{t})\|\Big]&<\|
abla f(w_{1})\|+ \sqrt{2L_{f}}\left(\sqrt{L_{f}+1}C^{1/3}_{v,d,3/2}(1+3\overline{M})^{2/3}+\sqrt{ rac{(L_{f}+1) eta_{1}^{2}}{2\alpha_{1}(1- eta_1)^{2}}+L_{f}|f^*|}ight)\&<+\infty. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the gradient supremum

nodes.name: Dominated convergence
nodes.statement: By combining the almost sure convergence result from Theorem \ref{thm:almost_sure} with the \emph{Lebesgue's Dominated Convergence} theorem, we obtain the $L_1$ convergence result, namely \[\lim_{t \rightarrow +\infty} \mathbb{E}[\|\nabla f(w_{t})\|] = 0. \tag*{\qedhere}\]
nodes.statement_short: Combine with Theorem 3.2

nodes.name: Property 4
nodes.statement: Due to Property \ref{property_3}, we have \begin{align*} \| m_{t}\|^{2}\le\beta_{1}\| m_{t-1}\|^{2}+(1-\beta_{1})\|g_{t}\|^{2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Norm recursion for m_t
nodes.section: D.1 Auxiliary Lemmas for Proving Lemma C.2

nodes.name: Rescale
nodes.statement: We multiply $1/\beta_{1}^{t}$ on the both sides of above inequality and obtain \begin{align*} \beta_{1}^{-t}\| m_{t}\|^{2}\le\beta_{1}^{-(t-1)}\| m_{t-1}\|^{2}+\beta_{1}^{-t}(1-\beta_{1})\|g_{t}\|^{2} , \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Multiply by beta_1^{-t}
nodes.section: D.1 Auxiliary Lemmas for Proving Lemma C.2

nodes.name: Iterate
nodes.statement: Iterating the above inequality, we acquire \begin{align*} \beta_{1}^{-t}\| m_{t}\|^{2}\le\| m_{0}\|^{2}+(1-\beta_{1})\sum_{k=1}^{t}\beta_{1}^{-k}\|g_{k}\|^{2}, \end{align*} that is \begin{align*} \|m_{t}\|^{2}&\le \beta_{1}^{t} \| m_{0}\|^{2}+(1-\beta_{1})\sum_{k=1}^{t}\beta_{1}^{t-k}\|g_{k}\|^{2}\\&=(1-\beta_{1})\sum_{k=1}^{t}\beta_{1}^{t-k}\|g_{k}\|^{2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Telescope to the first bound

nodes.name: Weighted version

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: In the final step \((a)\), we first apply Property \ref{property_-1} to bound \(\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}\|g_{t}\|^{2}]\) for all \( t \leq T \), by \(\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}(f(w_{t}) - f^*)]\) for \( t \leq T \). Then, using Equation (\ref{adam_w_2'}), we further bound \(\mathbb{E}[\Pi_{\Delta,t}(f(w_{t}) - f^*)]\) as \(\mathcal{O}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{T} \|\eta_{v_{t}} \circ g_{t}\|^{2}\right)\). Finally, we apply Equation (\ref{adam_w_2''}) to the previous summation. This completes the proof.
